newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures nudge up, but still directionless.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures nudge up, but still directionless.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures edged slightly higher during the London afternoon on Tuesday, lifted by a buoyant NYMEX crude, but the market was still seeking direction, brokers said.

By 1425 GMT the benchmark September Brent crude contract was 10 cents higher at $18.19 a barrel, while the front month gas oil contract remained unchanged from earlier levels at $163, up 50 cents on the day.
NYMEX crude was 8 cents higher at $19.26 a barrel, lifted by firm U.S. gasoline prices.
"Brent moved up a little when NYMEX opened slightly higher than expected, but the market is still stagnant and looking for direction," one broker said.
Gasoline prices in the U.S. have been firm in recent weeks on the back of the rising value of one of its blending components.
"The market is stagnant. There's very little going on. The market is yearning for direction," one broker said.
"A test of the lower range is favoured today, but there is no point getting too bearish while support levels hold," GNI Research said in a report.
GNI on Monday pegged potential support at $17.95, $17.85-80, $17.60, $17.45/50 and $17.30.
Brokers said news Iraq would on Tuesday formally present its aid distribution plan to the United Nations would not affect the market.
"It's an old story. The Iraq news is already built into the market," one broker said.
Prices were little moved on Monday when the U.N. said it had received a copy of Baghdad's aid plan. Acceptance of the plan was an Iraqi condition for the resumption of its crude exports.
Iraq needs to sell around 1.5 million barrels of crude per day to raise the $1 billion it needs to buy humanitarian aid before the deal ends in September.
The second phase of the oil-deal started on June 8.
